wins.claim: Full DXF import (splines, blocks, units) plus SVG and STL against LaserGRBL's single officially-'early' Inkscape-tuned SVG importer.
KerfDesk at least visualizes G-code (CNC preview, G2/G3, reimport-parity-tested); xTool Studio's documented import list opens nothing foreign.
Unit/DPI resolution, sanitization, malformed-file skip-and-report, and a perceptual import test versus SVG handled 'as is' with no text or fill.
Unmetered G-code/.rd/tiled export against Easel's tier-gated one-export-per-week free tier.

gaps.claim: No AI, PDF, EPS, CDR, or PLT import and no binary DXF versus the LightBurn/MillMage five-format engine.
PNG/JPG only; no BMP, GIF, TIFF, or WebP while every competitor imports at least four raster formats.
No .lbrn/.lbrn2 reader for the LightBurn-switcher persona, and the absence is un-ADR'd (severity bump per design 5.6).
SVG text and embedded images silently dropped with stale 'Phase D/E' toasts - an un-ADR'd divergence; LightBurn imports text with local fonts.
No clipboard-paste import, no Open Recent, and a three-way split import menu with an SVG-only Ctrl+I.
No artwork export at all (scene SVG/DXF/image out) - designs enter KerfDesk but never leave as vectors.
Unconditional replace-on-reimport with no add-as-copy option is an un-ADR'd divergence from LightBurn's add-a-copy default (S1-F5).
